The Information: DeepSeek seeks second funding round at a RMB 500 billion valuation after tenfold revenue growth

: Revenue reached RMB 475 million ($70.7 million) in January–July 2026, roughly 10 times its full-year 2025 revenue. Its net loss during the same period narrowed to RMB 715 million, compared with RMB 935 million for full-year 2025.

: Gross margin stood at 44.6%, with the API business posting an 82.9% gross margin. The high profitability was driven by AI infrastructure optimization, which enabled the company to run models on fewer chips while maintaining low inference costs.

: Revenue growth accelerated as global developer adoption of the recent V4 series, particularly V4-Flash, expanded. Annualized revenue reportedly rose to $400–500 million as of last month.

: DeepSeek also raised API prices to strengthen monetization. V4-Pro output pricing increased from $0.87 to $3.96 during peak hours and $1.98 during off-peak hours, but remains well below Kimi K3 at $15 and Claude Opus 5 at $25.

: AI infrastructure spending surged from RMB 1.2 billion in 2025 to RMB 11 billion in January–July this year, mainly due to increased server leasing and purchases of AI chips and computing equipment.

: Following its first external funding round in June, which raised RMB 50 billion, DeepSeek is now pursuing a second round to raise an additional RMB 50 billion at a RMB 500 billion valuation. It has also hired investment banks for a planned Shanghai IPO next year.
DeepSeek is reportedly looking to raise $7.4B at a $74 Billion valuation

BBG: DeepSeek plans to purchase more than 160,000 Huawei AI chips.

For now, DeepSeek does not plan to use Huawei chips for training.

DeepSeek wants to purchase more Huawei chips, but Huawei is currently constrained by limited production capacity.

Due to shortages of HBM and other memory components, Huawei’s production capacity for the 950DT is expected to be limited to only a few hundred thousand units this year.

It could take Huawei more than a year to fully meet DeepSeek’s orders.

If completed as planned, Inner Mongolia will become the key hub driving DeepSeek’s AI development.
